title: Gardenio — Latency & Cost Efficiency
description: The latency-and-cost companion board from the GRADE 2026-08-20 depth iteration (feature ka-0000003414; idea catalog docs/grafana-grade/2026-08-20T07:23:00Z/idea-catalog.md). It draws the live-but-undrawn latency histograms — user-request tail, reference-extract, mention cold-respawn SLO, respawn-phase breakdown, deferred-wait SLO, Jira issue-age, pod-phase transitions — beside the cost/cache efficiency levers: account cache-read-per-input, cost-per-bead-closed by project, compaction-vs-session-duration, operator-activity, and the upstream-error transition rate leading indicator. Every panel is grounded in a metric family with live series verified against gardenio-vmsingle this iteration.

options.content:
**Latency & cost efficiency** — the undrawn live latency histograms and the cost/cache-efficiency levers, carried from the GRADE 2026-08-20 idea catalog (`docs/grafana-grade/2026-08-20T07:23:00Z/idea-catalog.md`, ka-0000003414). Every panel is backed by a metric family with live series verified against gardenio-vmsingle this iteration.

**Live latency** — **#1** end-to-end user-request tail (`gardenio_user_request_latency_seconds`), **#2** reference-extract p50/p95/p99 (`gardenio_beads_references_extract_duration_seconds`), **#3** mention cold-respawn SLO (`gardenio_mention_cold_respawn_seconds`), **#4** respawn phase breakdown (`gardenio_slackbridge_respawn_phase_seconds`), **#7** deferred-wait SLO fan (`gardenio_agent_deferred_wait_seconds`), **#8** Jira issue-age profile (`gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds`), **#6** pod-phase transition timeline (`gardenio_agent_pod_phase_transitions_total`).

**Cost / cache efficiency** — **#5** account cache-read-per-input leaderboard (the prompt-cache cost lever), **#9** cost-per-bead-closed by project, **#10** compaction pressure vs median session duration (the context-tax correlation), **#11** operator-activity leaderboard, **#12** upstream-error TRANSITION rate — the smoother leading indicator the catalog flags over the intermittent `_active` gauge.

panels.title: #1 User-request latency heatmap (end-to-end tail)
panels.description: sum by (le) (rate(gardenio_user_request_latency_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])): the end-to-end user-facing request latency distribution across all surfaces/endpoints. A bright band drifting upward is the tail widening — slow page renders or daemon round-trips the p95 timeseries alone would smear. Bucket family is live but was undrawn as a heatmap before this board.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_user_request_latency_seconds_bucket samples in this range — no user-facing request was observed in the window. Widen the range; a persistently empty heatmap across a busy day means the histogram is not being emitted, so check up{component="agents"} on Gardenio — System Health.

panels.title: #8 Jira issue-age distribution heatmap
panels.description: sum by (le) (rate(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])): the age profile (now - created) of open Jira-bound work, as a snapshot histogram. Shows whether the backlog is skewing older over time. Only jira-metrics summary panels drew this family before.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket samples in this range — the jira-bridge age exporter published nothing in the window. Empty is NOT “no open Jira work”: a live exporter with no open issues renders a populated bottom bucket.

panels.title: #2 Reference-extract latency p50/p95/p99
panels.description: histogram_quantile over gardenio_beads_references_extract_duration_seconds_bucket: wall time to extract+replace bead_references rows for one mutation (regex pass + DELETE/INSERT round trip). Watches whether typed-mention/reference extraction keeps up as the bead graph grows.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_beads_references_extract_duration_seconds_bucket samples in this range — no bead mutation ran the reference-extract pass in the window, so the quantiles are UNDEFINED, not fast. Widen the range; if still empty, check up{component="beads"} on Gardenio — System Health.

panels.title: #3 Mention cold-respawn latency p95 (SLO 45s)
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95, ...) over gardenio_mention_cold_respawn_seconds_bucket: when an operator @-mentions a dark agent, seconds until it is live. The 45s dashed line is the SLO band (bucket set tops out at 180s). Live buckets, no dedicated panel before this.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_mention_cold_respawn_seconds_bucket samples in this range — no operator @-mention hit a dark agent in the window, so p95 is UNDEFINED, not within SLO. A low-volume family: widen the range before reading the empty panel as a pass.

panels.title: #4 Slack-bridge respawn phase p90 (dispatch vs boot)
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.90, ...) over gardenio_slackbridge_respawn_phase_seconds_bucket by (phase): which respawn phase — bridge-side dispatch (bead mint) vs pod-side boot (image pull + resume) — dominates thread-reply latency. phase enum: dispatch/boot/total.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_slackbridge_respawn_phase_seconds_bucket samples in this range — no Slack respawn happened in the window, so the dispatch/boot split is UNDEFINED. Widen the range; if still empty, check up{component="slack-bridge"} on Gardenio — System Health.

panels.title: #7 Deferred-wait latency p50/p90/p99 (SLO 1h)
panels.description: histogram_quantile over gardenio_agent_deferred_wait_seconds_bucket: time since bead creation for deferred/queued agents. The 3600s dashed line is the 1h SLO. A rising p99 means queued agents are waiting past SLO — agent-latency-distribution has a fan but no explicit SLO line.

defaults.noValue: gardenio_agent_deferred_wait_seconds_bucket returned nothing in this range. The likely reading is that no agent hit pool exhaustion in the window — but this panel cannot rule out a controller that is not exporting the histogram at all. Resolve with “#5 Reconcile dead-man — reconciles/min” on Gardenio — Fleet Capacity before recording this as a clean SLO.

panels.title: #6 Pod-phase transition rate (Pending→Running→Terminated)
panels.description: sum(rate(gardenio_agent_pod_phase_transitions_total[$__rate_interval])) by (phase_from, phase_to): where pods move in the lifecycle over time, as a state timeline. A persistent band on a from→to pair that is NOT Pending→Running (e.g. Pending stalling, Running→Failed) is a lifecycle problem forming. Complements fleet-capacity's flow-rate view with a time-aligned transition ribbon.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_pod_phase_transitions_total series — no agent pod changed phase since this controller booted. On an idle fleet this is legitimate; on a busy one it means the controller is dark (check up{component="agents"} on Gardenio — System Health).

panels.title: #5 Account cache-read per input token (cost lever)
panels.description: sum(gardenio_account_cache_read_tokens_current) by (account) / clamp_min(sum(gardenio_account_input_tokens_current) by (account),1): cache-read tokens served per fresh input token, per account — the prompt-cache cost lever. Higher = more of each prompt is being served from cache (cheaper). e2e/probe accounts filtered out.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_account_cache_read_tokens_current / _input_tokens_current series — the Anthropic rate-limit probe is not reporting, so cache amplification is UNKNOWN, not zero. Corroborate with “#12 Probe-loop dead-man” on Gardenio — Control-plane Liveness.

panels.title: #11 Operator-activity leaderboard (top 10)
panels.description: topk(10, sum(gardenio_beads_created_by_operator_total) by (operated_by)): which operators drive the most agent work, by beads created. The metric's label is operated_by (human id, or agent/system/fleet/unknown).

defaults.noValue: gardenio_beads_created_by_operator_total returned nothing. This counter is created on its first bead.created event, so empty means either no bead has been created since the beads daemon last restarted, or the daemon is not being scraped — it never means operators were idle. Resolve with up{component="beads"} on Gardenio — System Health.

panels.title: #9 Cost per bead closed, by project ($/bead)
panels.description: sum(rate(gardenio_agent_spend_usd_total[1h])) by (project) / clamp_min(sum(rate(gardenio_beads_events_total{event="closed"}[1h])) by (project),0.001): hourly spend divided by beads closed, per project — which project spends most per unit of delivered work. cost-overview has the fleet headline but not this per-project trend.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_spend_usd_total series in this range — spend is UNKNOWN, so $/bead cannot be computed and empty must NOT be read as $0. The denominator is clamped, so a live spend series with zero closes still draws a line; empty means the spend emitter itself is silent.

panels.title: #10 Compaction pressure vs median session duration
panels.description: Left axis: sum(gardenio_agent_compactions_current) — total live context compactions. Right axis: histogram_quantile(0.5, ...) over gardenio_agent_session_duration_seconds_bucket — median session length. Do long sessions drive compactions (a cost/latency tax)? The two series riding together is the signal.

defaults.noValue: neither gardenio_agent_compactions_current nor gardenio_agent_session_duration_seconds_bucket has data in this range — no agent is compacting AND no session completed in the window. If only the duration line is missing, widen the range; a total blank means the controller is not being scraped.

panels.title: #12 Upstream-error transition rate by category (leading indicator)
panels.description: sum(rate(gardenio_agent_upstream_error_transitions_total[$__rate_interval])) by (category): rate of agents ENTERING an upstream Claude-error category (edge-triggered counter). The catalog flags this as a smoother leading indicator than the intermittent point-in-time gardenio_agent_upstream_error_active gauge (advice ka-0000005924: the two must reconstruct each other). Catalog #12 also suggests siting a copy on system-health beside leg-A.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_upstream_error_transitions_total series — no agent has ENTERED an upstream provider error since this controller booted, so the counter was never created. Healthy; it lights up on the first entry.
